blocks.body:
This is a 12-week program built around a simple idea: sexual performance responds to training the same way strength or endurance does. Nothing here involves medication, a consultation, or anyone else seeing your data. It's you, working through a structured program at your own pace.

The program has three threads that run in parallel: pelvic floor training, body-level changes (movement, sleep, alcohol), and mind-level changes (breathing, easing performance pressure). Most sessions take 5–10 minutes.

Missing a day doesn't cost you anything — you'll pick up right where you left off, not where the calendar says you should be.

sessions.title: Finding the muscle
sessions.intent: Learn to isolate the pelvic floor before training it

blocks.body:
Before any training, you need to find the right muscle — most people who try pelvic floor exercises on their own never do, and end up working the wrong thing for weeks.

An easy way in: next time you're urinating, try to stop the flow partway through, then let it go again. The muscle that does that is the one you're training. Don't make a habit of doing this during urination itself — it's a one-time locator, not a drill.

Once you can feel it: you should notice a lift-and-squeeze, roughly between your sit bones. Your stomach, thighs, and glutes should stay relaxed — if your whole body is tensing, you've found the wrong muscle.

If you can't feel anything distinct after a few tries, that's common and not a problem — the next few sessions will keep giving you ways in.

sessions.title: Sleep and blood flow
sessions.intent: See why sleep is part of a sexual performance program

blocks.body:
It's not an obvious connection, but sleep is one of the more consistent factors in sexual performance research. Erections partly depend on healthy blood vessel function, and poor sleep is linked to lower testosterone and reduced blood vessel responsiveness over time.

You don't need a perfect routine. The aim here is just to notice your pattern — the log below takes five seconds and builds a picture over the coming weeks that you'll see on your progress chart.

sessions.title: Alcohol, honestly
sessions.intent: Understand alcohol's short-term effect without cutting anything out

blocks.body:
Alcohol is a depressant — in the short term it dampens the nervous system signals involved in arousal, on top of any longer-term effects on blood flow. Most men have noticed this at some point without connecting it to a pattern.

This program isn't asking you to quit anything. The daily log just tracks drinks alongside your other numbers, so if there's a pattern for you specifically, it becomes visible instead of anecdotal.

sessions.title: Week one, done
sessions.intent: Close the week and see what's next

blocks.body:
One week in. The foundation phase runs through week four — the aim isn't intensity yet, it's building a pattern you'll actually keep. From next week, sets get a little longer and the breathing work shifts toward performance-anxiety situations specifically rather than general wind-down.

If you've missed a day already, that's normal and doesn't reset anything — you're exactly where you are.
